title: Sohra: Cradle of Rain and Cascades (Ka Sohra)
cultural_context: Poetic ode to Sohra (Cherrapunji), renowned for roaring waterfalls, swirling mist, and historic kings.
lyrics_khasi:
Ko Sohra, ko hima ka mariang,
Haba u lyoh u sop ia ki kliar,
Ki kshaid jong pha ki pashat rupa
Sha ki them ba jylliew bad jngai;
Pha long ka kmie jong ki puriskam,
Ka shnong ki syiem ba radbah,
Ha pneh jong pha u slap u theh
Kupar ba kynrei na bneng.

Nohsngithiang bad Nohkalikai
Ki kiew kum ki khlur ba sawa,
Ki mawlynnai ha them Shella
Ki phriang la ka jingphyrnai;
Sah junom, ko Sohra ba suk,
Ha dohnud jong ngi ba rwai,
Ka ri ka burom bad ka akor
Ba ri u Hynniew Trep.
lyrics_english:
O Sohra, realm of sacred nature,
When thick mists blanket your crests,
Your cascades splash ribbons of silver
Down into deep, distant canyons;
You are mother to ancient fables,
Seat of legendary kings,
Into your lap the rains pour down
Bountiful blessings from heaven.

Nohsngithiang and Nohkalikai falls
Roar forth like singing stars,
The limestone jewels of Shella canyon
Spreading their radiant glow;
Abide forever, tranquil Sohra,
In our hearts as we sing,
Land of nobility and decorum
Guarded by the Seven Huts.
